utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, are you ready for your witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Like with the previous witnesses, face distortion and a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections? Mr. Stringer? Mr. Scott? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not really. It's not clear to the Prosecution why such a man would need protection but we won't oppose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So the request is granted. Mr. Usher could we have the witness, please. [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please take the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: A few instructions that I normally give to every witness. Whatever you say is being interpreted, so try to find a certain pace, a certain speed, so that you do not speak too slow or too fast. The best procedure for you would be to look at the dot on the screen and when the dot stops, start giving your answer. In this courtroom, we are all going to call you Witness NM, and you make sure that you do not say anything that would reveal your identity because protection measures have been granted for you. Do you understand? Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, I would kindly ask the usher to give you the name -- the piece of paper with your name, if that indeed is your name, then just say yes. You can lean back in the chair, approach the microphone so that you can feel comfortable.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's start. Introduce yourself to this Chamber without saying your name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to private session just in case? Private session means that only us, only we in the courtroom can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind and very briefly, as I want to get to the point as soon as possible, and to the facts that I want to discuss with you, can you just briefly describe for the Chamber the situation in Siroki Brijeg did you manage to defend it and save it and then can you please continue by telling me something about the end of 1992 and liberation of Mostar? Just briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: After the shelling of Siroki Brijeg, the situation was psychotic, a lot of population had to be evacuated towards Croatia. At the time, people who were at the forefront of the municipal staff, I mean Mr. Naletilic, Mladen Naletilic, who was -- who had arrived from the west, and to my mind, he was -- he, there, he had learned about freedom the way it existed in the west, and who played a major role in the organisation of the defence of Siroki Brijeg, especially at that time when the situation was so bad in Siroki Brijeg, after the shelling, given that the Serbian army was so close.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind and tell us whether you participated in the operation of the "June Dawn"? What was that operation? Were you a member of any unit and if you were, what unit was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. I did participate in the June Dawn operation. That operation was an operation to liberate Mostar. The boundaries of Siroki Brijeg, Citluk, Capljina, Stolac municipalities, I participated as a member in the Convicts Battalion on the axis, on the liberation axis which was assigned to the municipal staff of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this unit, the Convicts Battalion? Who was its head? Did you have any specific task in that operation? Who was leading you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion was a unit composed of volunteers, which was composed of volunteers from Siroki Brijeg municipality, who had some previous war experiences because they had already been active as volunteers in late 1991, in the southern theatre, war theatre, in the vicinity of Dubrovnik, and as such, they organised this unit, the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber who was the founder of the Convicts Battalion, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I believe that one has to emphasise the role of Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Mr. Zarko Odak, Mr. Ludvig Pavlovic, Mr. Ivan Andabak, Mr. Tomas, Mr. Mikulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you have any idea why it got the name the Convicts Battalion? Can you please explain to the Chamber? Maybe you have your interpretation of that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: My interpretation and my opinion why the unit was called the Convicts Battalion is this: This unit had a psychological effect when -- with regard to the enemy, and its name, the convicts, were meant to deter the forces of evil, which wanted to devastate the -- whatever good was there, for the Croatian people. When I say "the convicts," I mean that the biggest punishment for the aggressor would have been to lose either a battle or the war. On the other hand, at the time, the public opinion and the information that I had at the time were such that the name is -- was given to the Convicts Battalion because it was organised by the people who had been politically persecuted during the communist regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's go back to that operation to liberate Mostar. In that operation, the Convicts Battalion, did it have a commander? If it did, who was its commander? And was the operation completed successfully?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The municipal staff had a specific task during the operation, June Dawn and the task for the Convicts Battalion was to take the key feature, sorry, Orlovac, after which they were to continue combat operations in order to take the features together with the Mostar forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay, then. I have to interrupt you. So the operation ended successfully. You did not tell me whether the battalion had a commander and who was its commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At the time, the head of the Convicts Battalion was Mr. Naletilic. There was also Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very often, we have heard in this courtroom, on -- this was said by my colleagues, "the officers of the Convicts Battalion." Did the Convicts Battalion ever have officers? If it did, when was that and how many commanders were there in the Convicts Battalion, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At the time, that is at the beginning of the war in Herzegovina, there were no officers at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Later on, when the home guard brigades were organised, then the first ranks were awarded and this was published in the public gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I think it was at the beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let us clear up this matter straight away. If you please, who commanded the Convicts Battalion? How many commanders were there? Who were those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: In the first place, I mean Mr. Naletilic. Clearly, there was also Andabak there, and it was coordinated through the municipal staff, those people that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did this command structure change over time or did it always remain the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: After the liberation operations of the boundaries of the municipality of Siroki Brijeg, the liberation of Mostar, and predominant facilities in the directions of Gacko and Nevesinje, the mountain Velez, Bijelo Polje and Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We'll come back to that later. Will you please answer my question first. So the question was did the command structure change and, if you can briefly tell the -- Their Honours what you know about that? And whenever you mention months, then tell us also years to avoid any objections by the Prosecution and also full names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The command structure in the Convicts Battalion in August, September, perhaps October of that same year, 1992, during the conflict, during the struggle, a number of lads had matured, who were selected -- who came out by natural selection, who gained authority in those battles, and there, Mr. Mario Hrkac, Predrag Mandic, Stanislav Kraljevic, and a number of other lads stand out in particular. But sometime, therefore in September or October, Mario Hrkac became the commander of the Convicts Battalion, clearly along side Mr. Andabak, who was always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in 1992, they were the only commanders, there were no other commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At that time, they were the only commanders, and there were no other commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was that the situation in 1993, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, we heard in this courtroom that Mr. Andabak was an alcoholic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, sir, that was not true. Mr. Andabak suffered from diabetes. He was very gravely ill and he was not an alcoholic at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did he get insulin every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, he took insulin every day, and we knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at that time, do you know, at that time, I mean, 1992 and 1993, do you know something about the funding? I do not mean only the Convicts Battalion but all the units, how were the units funded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At that time, the municipal staff, in January, the municipal staffs which were in operation, in those municipalities where the Croats constituted the majority in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was the municipal staffs which at that time in the early stage and later on, when the organisation became better, the municipal staffs started doing it for the major part in those early days and the logistics centre in Grude were the one who is did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What period of time did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: 1992 and I also believe later on in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, can you tell us what units are there in Siroki Brijeg, apart from the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At that time, if you are talking about 1992, the Siroki Brijeg, that is the municipal staff, which coordinated all these activities had three battalions, Poskok, Convicts Battalions and those who roughly be the units that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine. Tell us, where were you quartered as soldiers, that is those others and the Convicts Battalion in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Those were volunteer units at that time. There were no military facilities in the municipality of Siroki Brijeg. There are about 20.000, 30.000 inhabitants and they practically had no army structure so all of the men, all the units spent nights at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. And tell us, please, did you have lineups, hoisting up, saluting the flags, in a facility of a kind called the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. What lineup? At that time there were no lineups, no reviews, no salutes to the flag. It wasn't organised at that level. Those were all the embryonic stages of the organisation so that there were no reviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Not even in 1993. There was nothing of that in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were there any prisons in the tobacco station? I mean we heard here in the courtroom that there was some kind of prison in the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, I don't recall any prison. I don't think there was any prison in the tobacco station at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you have your command there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, in the tobacco station, or rather in the compound of that tobacco station, there was this building where we were -- where the Convicts Battalion had its makeshift command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good. Fine. Now, tell me, if you know when and where did the unit called Baja Kraljevic originate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I know that because I was a member of that unit at the time. So it was born after the liberation operations against the Serbs and the battles fought to liberate Mostar. And after that, I believe it was decided at a higher level that is at the Main Staff of the ministry, to set up for that area for that zone, a special purposes unit, and since we were given a military facility with proper infrastructure in the Heliodrom camp, which was on the way, which was on the way in which the units of the Convicts Battalion were progressing, when they were liberating Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. We heard here that Baja Kraljevic was part of the Convicts Battalion. So my question is Baja Kraljevic parts of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is not true that the Baja Kraljevic unit is a part of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just briefly, when did it happen, which year? Will you please explain to the court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is 1992 that -- as I've already said, that after the fighting for liberation in June or perhaps late June and perhaps in the beginning of July, Baja Kraljevic unit was established and it had its military post code and that is 1724. The military code of the Convicts Battalion, post code of the Convicts Battalion was 1717. So that absolutely these two units had nothing in common except that about ten of us members of the Convicts Battalion joined that unit in the very early day. Mr. Predrag Mandic was appointed the commander and I was an instructor. I was responsible for the drills and was the deputy commander of -- deputy commander in charge of those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, could you be issued any orders by Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. At that time, Mr. Naletilic did not command. Sometimes in September or October or perhaps August of 1992, he was no longer the commander of the Convicts Battalion, because we all knew that he had a serious lung complaint, so that Mario Hrkac Cikota was appointed the commander. About ten of us went and a new unit set up so we contributed to the development of a new unit, and no front line commander or anything could have Mr. Naletilic above him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I didn't understand this passage. Was Mr. Naletilic the commander or not in September or October? Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So will you please slow down? Because Her Honour is receiving interpretation in French, which is being taken from English so, you know...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Mladen Naletilic, at that time, I'm not sure whether it was September or October, but he stopped being the commander of the Convicts Battalion. That was that time, September or October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Your Honours, my apologies, we meant the command structure of Baja Kraljevic and the witness's identity could be disclosed. We are so concerned with moving ahead and performing well that we forget about these things. Please take care, if you are referring to your office, to your duties, then please say so in advance so that we can ask for a private session, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell Their Honours what was the chain of command? Who would issue orders to Baja Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Right. At the levels, the Tiers that were above us were the Main Staff, the ministry and the Presidency, and we were attached as an unit to an area of responsibility in Southeast Herzegovina, and when we would go to a particular area of responsibility, we would then be seconded, we would be attached to the commanders of those areas. So there we would be under the command of the commander to whose area of responsibility we have come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was the nature of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: That was an intervention unit, where the front line was under threat Baja Kraljevic unit would come to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where is the Convicts Battalion now and what is its nature now, right let's move on to 1993 and let's stick to 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion remained in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was its nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Well, same, it continued as an intervention unit and following the chain of command as I have just told you, there were superior tiers, and that was how Baja Kraljevic unit operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Do you know -- I mean do you personally know, and let's start with May, June, 1993, to the end of that year, did you meet up with the Convicts Battalion? Did you engage in any joint actions? If yes, where was that, generally, what you know personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. We had our joint combat operations but I think that the Convicts Battalion, after the attack and aggression by the MOS forces on the 30th of June, 1993, on Bijelo Polje, North Camp, suburban parts of the town of Mostar, after that the intervention unit was in sector north, and sector north was a part o the operative zone East Herzegovina, which was split down into three zones, sector north, sector of city defence and sector south. So that the intervention units at different periods of time, had their areas of responsibility where they undertook intervention operations, and I remember this particular date because at that time, with the Baja Kraljevic unit, I went, as an intervention unit, to Bijelo Polje, which had been attacked, and I stayed there with the unit for some 20, 25 days. And that, at the time, in the area of Djubrani, there were -- there was the Convicts Battalion as the intervention unit in the area of responsibility of the Siroki Brijeg Brigade, and I believe that it stayed there right up to the end of 1993, perhaps November or December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please, be so kind as to tell this Court, this Honourable Court, how long, to your knowledge, did the Convicts Battalion exist? Or rather -- no, let's not talk about the Convicts Battalion. Perhaps I'll later come to Baja Kraljevic again, you already mentioned this in the beginning so will you please explain the Honourable Court whether the Convicts Battalion ceased to exist formally and if so, when? And what kind of reorganisation was that, which year, which month?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I need this to be redacted or perhaps we should go into private session, just in case, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the Convicts Battalion ceased to exist, Mr. Andabak, who -- and he was there at the time, I believe he was assigned to the Main Staff or the Defence Ministry. And this -- and those men who were members of the units, they were given the opportunity to join guards brigades. Naturally, with the clearly defined organisation, where everything went according to the book, and there was the book, and with all the necessary documents existed, so such a guard brigade which was in terms of its organisation was to have about 3500 people, and it could accommodate everybody who wanted to become a professional soldier. Clearly, if that individual met the criteria, which at that time had been laid down for that particular formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate that you were a witness of your time and I am very happy that I could get you here and ask you to explain certain things to the Honourable Court because I see that you were in that area for the duration. So I will ask you now a couple of more questions in order to try to draw a more precise picture. We've seen many documents but I will not waste my time on that because I presume that my learned friend will do that. In many documents, we saw Tuta ATG, and then Tuta's units, then references in 1993, personally, to commander Mladen Naletilic. So my first question is whether there was any such thing as Tuta ATG.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: There was never such thing as the Tuta ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you then have some explanation for that? How can one then see, have references to the Tuta ATG or to him as a commander? And you told us that he was not a commander in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, and that is true. However, since at that time that I was talking about, the liberation operations, June Dawn, Mr. Mladen Naletilic's role in that operation, to all intensive purposes he was, at the time, considered as one of the key people in the liberation of that area, parts of the municipality of Siroki Brijeg, and the town itself. Of course, together with all the other men and units from Mostar, Siroki Brijeg and those other municipalities, Capljina, Citluk and so on and so forth. So that he was held in high regard and respected, and people of the area were no end grateful to him. And as regards the Tuta ATG, and

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: [redacted] It is more out of respect, it is for the sake of the time we spent together, which was sealed with blood. And that is how in 1992, we called Mr. Naletilic commander, and so on and so forth. And especially it found its reflection in that later stage, in 1993, when --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I was about to ask you, sorry to interrupt you, so how did you address, if you met Mr. Naletilic in 1994, 1995, how would you address him? Or other soldiers, other military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Well, it is precisely that team from that time, there was always warmth, there was always friendliness, commander, and within that context, and I can give you an example, I still, when I, for instance, meet the Minister of Defence of the federation from the time, Mr. Vlado Soljic, and still say, "Mr. Minister, shall we go and have some coffee," even though he's not been a minister for six or seven years now but at the time when these areas were liberated he was a minister and so when we meet, I still Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. say, "Mr. Minister." My men and my officers commander, address me as commander even though I left them some five, six, no, seven years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Do you know who Tutici, "Tuta's boys" are, did anyone refer to you as Tuta's boys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Oh, come, no, never, ever did anyone call me that or that team of the Convicts Battalion. Nobody ever called them that. But I will allow that it is possible that there were people at the time, when the misuse began, you know how it happens, when you acquire your authority by your deeds and since Mr. Mladen Naletilic was a warm-hearted man, as he treated well those men who were volunteers, not only in the Convicts Battalion, and other units too and they approached him for some assistance, he was always ready to help those people who had come to seek some assistance, but in my opinion, it was largely misused by some other people who followed a different motive. Clearly there were some who needed assistance but it grew into a habit then which then culminated in different details, in here in such a manner of communication, so when somebody says we are Tutici they go to a municipality and say we are Tuta's boys, Tuta sent us and so on and so forth, in order to solicit something, to get something, to get out of -- from other people at the same time on -- because of that name, while at the same time Tuta and his men know nothing about that. I know there were cases of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber whether it was true that the goal, the objective of the Convicts Battalion and Mladen Naletilic was to expel Muslims from the area where they -- there were conflicts during 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is an insult, it's out of the question to say that the goal of Kaznjenicka Bojna, of the Convicts Battalion, or any other unit of the Croatian Defence Council would be ethnic cleansing and expelling Muslims from the area of any municipality or any town at the time. That is not true. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was the position of Mr. Naletilic on the war with Muslims? Do you know, if you socialised with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm to this Chamber that Mr. Naletilic, on a number of occasions when we met each other, and I know that he said that to other people as well, that he absolutely advocated the unity of Muslims and Croats. He was simply a person who belonged to that sort, as we say, in Mostar, and nobody from that area, at the time, nobody understood what was going on when the first conflict started. Nobody realised that this would escalate, and become a war, a full-blown war between Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that he belonged to the kind of people that we call down there the Croat of the old kind. This did not enter the transcript the first time. Can you please just in one sentence tell us what did you mean by saying a Croat of the old kind, of the old grand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: That is what we say about those people who advocated the joint life of Croats and Muslims, Croats and Muslims living together, and this arose from the historical life, joint life, of Croats and Muslims in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I would now move on to my last two topics, the first one would be did you participate in the operation in April, 1993, the operation that took place in Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I did participate in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Chamber what you saw? Because we are all very interested in that. From the beginning to the very end. I'll try not to interrupt you. If necessary, I will maybe guide you through your testimony by some subquestions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At the time, in April, 1993, as far as I can remember, I was in charge of the drill, the drills in the Baja Kraljevic unit, whose commander I was at the time, and on the 17th of April, on behalf of the operation zone Southeastern Herzegovina, we were given the full combat readiness order. I believe that this was one or two hours -- two hours after midnight. At the time, we stayed in the barracks, Mr. Baja Kraljevic and myself. And then around 4.00 or 5.00 in the morning, we received another call from the duty operations officer, and I believe it was Mr. Raguz of the Southeastern Herzegovina operations zone, and that we were ordered to go, as an intervention unit, to the Sovici and Doljani sector. We also received information that there had been aggression against the Croatian areas that we are supposed to be in full combat readiness and that the attack is to be expected precisely on that axis, the Sovici Doljani axis or sector. In the early morning hours of that day, Mr. Mandic and myself and some of the troops which at the time were in the barracks, half of the troops were at home at the time, so we.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can I please interrupt you? Are you familiar with this order? Is that the order? This is Exhibit D1/107.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please, Mr. Usher, show it to the witness? We all have it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I have never seen this order, but it does confirm that the information that we received from the operations, duty operations officer, about the open aggression of Muslims, that all the units were in full combat readiness, that all the leaves were to be terminated, that a battalion from Posusje was being sent towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. You don't have to read the document. It speaks for itself, and that the additional units were being mobilised in Siroki Brijeg, Ljubuski, Citluk. Whose order is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: This is the order of the Chief of the Main Staff to all the operation zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. You may continue, be as concise as possible. I know it is not easy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: In the early morning hours, we departed on the axis Mostar-Siroki Brijeg-Posusje and arrived at the Risovac sector where one part of the troops of the Posusje Battalion, the Siroki Brijeg Battalion had been already. There were some other troops. I don't know who they were. I can't remember. In contact with them, in order to gain as much information, we tried to find out what the situation was, what it was all about, because we did not have enough information. We thought some -- somebody would arrive and that we would be given a specific task. It was said to us that on behalf of the Posusje Battalion, one of their groups, a dozen of them, had left from Sovicka Vrata towards the BH Army checkpoint which was visibly reinforced by the Muslim forces between Sovici and Sovicka Vrata. As they were descending, mortar fire was opened on that group, and on the general area below Sovicka Vrata towards the road that we had taken to arrive. Obviously, since we had received information from the people who were up there that the battles, that the terrible aggression took place in the area of Konjic municipality, on the villages with the Croatian population, they were killed and injured in the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, on the strength of which was the Mijat Tomic Battalion in the region of Doljani. When the fire was opened, Mr. Mandic and myself, went with some of our troops, Mr. Mario Hrkac, with the troops in the Convicts Battalion, we said to the lads, to the lads from these municipal battalions, the Siroki Brijeg and Posusje Battalion and other units who were there, that we would be -- we would take the most difficult axis and that we would undertake the necessary operation in order to take those facilities which were the key facilities towards Sovicka Vrata and the valley between, Cvrsnica, and together with our units, the Baja Kraljevic and the Convicts Battalion, we went on the axis Strazbenica Pasije Stijene, where the fire line and the fire points were -- belonged to the MOS forces. We engaged in combat, and sometime in the afternoon, around 1600 hours, I believe that we took the area of Pasije Stijene. We continued on the axis along the Bacina Mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise, I have to interrupt you. We are in the break time already, unless the Honourable Court wants us to finish this topic. And then make a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to finish this topic at least so that the transcript is consistent. And by the way, how long are you going to take, Mr. Krsnik, in your direct examination, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It won't take long. I started at 9.11 and I believe that I will need another 15 or 20 minutes, not more, because I would like to start my next witness today. Maybe we won't be able to finish that witness but at least I want to finish my examination-in-chief of that next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness finish this topic, then we'll break. Then you will take about 10 to 15 minutes to wind up your direct examination. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After we took Pasije Stijene, that was on the 17th, we continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I again apologise for the interruption. I will ask the usher in order to provide the Honourable Court with the insight into what you're describing, I am tendering 6.2 and 6.3, and 8.2. I have in hand in case our Madam Registrar doesn't have them. Please take the pointer. Whenever you mention a feature or a place, you can point them to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please can you put these photos on the ELMO, put them on the ELMO? And the witness will choose --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, when you talk about features or sites, can you please choose the photo and show us what you're talking about? You can actually show -- point on the photos.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I believe that this is Sovici village, and this northern part here, from the west, this is the area of Pasije Stijene, and further down, there is Sovicka Vrata. We were behind Strazbenica. We came to Pasije Stijene. That is west of Sovici. We proceeded towards the northern part of Sovici, towards the Bacina Planina Pass, towards Rama, and we continued along the Bacina Planina, on the rims downwards, towards --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: There are other photos. Maybe you can show us on those photos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I think we can best see it on this photo. I believe that this is the other side of Bacina Mountain. Here you can see the road between Doljani and Sovici, and we continued taking features, Pomen, Oklanica, Pisvir, 944, which I believe is somewhere here, and downwards towards 902, and then we descended to Kosna Luka. This lasted for some -- it was on the 17th, 18th and 19th, when we descended along this axis. In the meantime, we heard that after the first day, the commander of the battalion, who had organised this fire line, and who had organised this line to -- facing the units of the Croatian Defence Council, and if you look at the valley between Bacina Mountain and Cvrsnica, you can see that this is the area, if that -- if you can take a Bacina Mountain and Sovicka Vrata that this is the area from which you can feed your troops and this is an exit towards Posusje and further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, let's go back and concentrate in order to finish this topic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You heard that somebody had surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, the commander, Mr. Ovnovic, I believe that he was the commander of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear that or did you witness that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, I didn't witness that because me -- I and Mr. Mandic and Mr. Hrkac, we were on this axis, but I heard it on the Motorola, that he had surrendered, and that the battalion had surrendered in Sovici, and their command and the troops. We continued towards -- and during these three days, somewhere around here, around Ilijina Grude, that is a rock below Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you show it on the photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: You can't see it too well but roughly it is below these peaks, if this is Pomen, Oklanica, Pisvir, Ilijina Gruda is somewhere around here. From these hill tops, some of the troops from our units were descending and met sniper fire or some other burst, and Mate Markic and Goran Andric were killed by that fire, and then somewhere below Kosna Luka and then further on towards Jablanica, that was one day after the 19th, in the afternoon, that was when Boka Barbaric, a member of the Convicts Battalion got killed. Since we had three killed and several wounded, and since we had the task in this operation to -- since our task was completed, a team came and pulled out Mr. Boka Barbaric's body, and Mr. Mandic and I remained for a while in order to introduce the home guard units. We remained there for a very short while. We arrived in Doljani village around 5.00 in the afternoon, 5.00 or 6.00 in the afternoon. And when we got there, we saw that there were troops there. We saw Mr. Mladen Naletilic, because somebody had already informed him, somebody had already fetched him, somebody had already informed him that Boka Barbaric had got killed. Boka Barbaric was one of those who had joined the battalion very early on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just briefly, what happened next? And did you and your unit and the Convicts Battalion, during these operations, ever enter Sovici village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. We didn't. We took the features north and northwest of Sovici and towards Jablanica. We took them one by one and we could not go down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My learned friend is going to examine you on that. What happened next? You pulled down the dead bodies, you saw Mr. Naletilic, and what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Our unit withdrew, we withdrew to Siroki Brijeg. Mario Hrkac remained below Kosna Luka and towards the elevation 902, he said he would man the line there, that his home guards would man the line, that there was no need for all of us to remain there and that he would join us in Siroki. We went towards --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Just tell us where you went and where -- when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: We went towards Siroki Brijeg. We stopped in Risovac because Mr. Naletilic was in the car in front of us. He stopped for a moment to tell us that he would go and pick up his children at Mate Zelenika's place. That is on the main way towards Posusje. Actually 200, 300 metres off that road. That was where the Mate Zelenika's house was. And then he told us that we would meet in Boka Barbaric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where is Boka Barbaric's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The house is very close. It is in the neighbourhood where Mr. Naletilic lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we have finished there topic. After this we are going to say a few words about Rastani and I will wind up with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we have ten minutes still and I'd lake to complete your examination today so please be very specific and brief. Do you know anything about the 23rd of September, 1993, and so-called Rastani operation, that is Rastani front line? What do you know about that, briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: On the 23rd of September, I know that the Baja Kraljevic unit was tasked with intervening, with carrying out an intervention action, in the area of responsibility of sector north, on the Goranci, Jedrinje, Djubrani line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, will you slow down to make things easier for us, Goranci, Djubrani, Jedrinje, J-E-D-R-I-N-J-E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: And I remember exactly the task with which we were issued by the sector commander. And that order said that we were to link up with the Siroki Brijeg Brigade in the area of Jedrinje facing Bucici, to pull out the casualties and fatalities and set up the front line and bring in the forces of the Siroki Brijeg Brigade. And he told me that in the early hours of the morning on that same day, along Djubrani, Goranci, Golubic, Velika, Mala, Vlajina or Arapovo Brdo, a unit of the Convicts Battalion had been sent to that area, because in that area, the -- it was to be the link up with the Siroki Brijeg Brigade and that that area, front line had been attacked, so the Convicts Battalion went there for an intervention action, and we stayed there for about four or five days. And during those four or five days, we mopped up the ground and I remember exactly how we entered Jedrinje, because there were dead and wounded there, and I remember how we found there wounded who was alive, Robert Primorac, who had studied with me in Zagreb at some point in time. He had lost a finger and he also had a -- was wounded in the leg, and he was so muddled that he did not know whose troops had arrived, ours or Muslim forces. He was in shock. He was all muddled. There were dead bodies around him. And he had spent the night there on the front line, and said that there were a number of lads who had been taken away, captured, in that operation. We had, I believe, two dead and six or seven wounded lads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. And my one-but-last question. Was there a commander of the Rastani front line and if so, who was that and when was he appointed to that post and meanwhile, I will ask for Exhibit D1/390.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. There was the commander, as far as I can remember. I believe that at that time, that at that time it was the area of responsibility of the city defence, if this is September, of those three sectors that I mentioned before, this was the city defence sector, and that as this order here says, that Colonel Milan Stampar is appointed the commander of the Rastani front line and that all the units in the Rastani area are to be subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You can look at this order, are you familiar with it, it must be it, then, are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with this order but it is Mr. Stampar, it concerns Mr. Stampar and I know that he commanded the Rastani front line and all the units who would go to that particular area would then be attached to him, that is subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, it says something here, IZM Djubrani, what does it mean, IZM?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: IZM means forward command post Djubrani. Djubrani is a rather large area so IZM means forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Forward command post, very good. Will you just read to me, please, the date of this document, D1/390?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The 25th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. Do you know Ralf Rudiger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he ever a member of your unit in Baja Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, he was not a member of Baja Kraljevic, because he did not meet the criteria. He was rather prone to alcohol and so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I believe in 1992 sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Now can I ask Madam Registrar for my last question, for Exhibit P704? It is said that this is the list of all the members of the Convicts Battalion. So will you please look at it, just the names and please comment on it. It is said here that this is the payroll of December, the 2nd of December, 1993, for November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: As this is here indicated I do not know what this means, what these groups mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, just leaf through the list and if you see some name --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Here in the command, Zeljko Ravic. Josip Bosnjak, at that time was a deputy. I commanded the 3rd Brigade of Mostar HVO and Zeljko Bosnjak was my deputy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the 3rd Brigade, you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, right, go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I don't know what these ranks here mean next to names. Captain, captain, because at that time, there were no ranks in units. Otherwise, it would have been carried by Narodni Novine, by the Official Gazette, had there been any ranks. I don't know what these groups mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: From what I know, Zeljko Vukoja came after Mario Hrkac was killed, that he became the operative commander of the Convicts Battalion along side Andabak, of course. This here, these people, I have no idea who these are. This group 4, I have no idea who these people are. Group 5, I have no idea what -- what these groups mean. Uh-huh, here is Andabak. That's all right. Culafic, Kontosic, I have no idea who these people are. Ivan Hrkac, I know him. It's a man who at that time worked for the police on Hvar, we are good friends and I know that. Danko Pilnovac is the chief of police in Siroki Brijeg so that he couldn't be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, there are also some female names. Do you know them, on the first page, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you both of you. That was my memory. That's why I was wondering about the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There are some Defence bundles of documents that should be distributed. They are already -- have they gone out? I assume that the Chamber's have been distributed as well. Mr. President, let me explain to hopefully avoid confusion. There are two separate bundles and it is -- there is no magic to it except that it came a point in time in preparation it was easier to divide them into two separate bundles. The first bundle that I'll be dealing with the first bundle that I'll be dealing with starts with Exhibit P173.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is absolutely unacceptable. Yes, the examination may go on, I don't object to that, but that we get binders and that the Prosecutor uses some 15 documents dated 1991 -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really think what, and then we shall say we shall all wrap it in the gift paper of credibility and what? Do not interrupt me, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have a witness present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do not allow the Prosecutor to interrupt me when I'm speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand you object to the bundle of documents furnished by the Prosecution but if in the Rules there is no limitation of presenting the documents to this courtroom. Some documents may be recently issued but it might be relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, can we then know when is it exactly that the Prosecutor came by those documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you could raise your objections to this document but do not go into the details, because we have the witness in the courtroom. And he has not been cross-examined yet. You have to understand that we only admit the document after the witness is out of the courtroom. We understand that you object the use of this document but I'm sorry to say that there is no limitations in the Rules forbidding any document that is used. When it comes to the points of admission of those documents, you may raise your objections. Let's see what the Prosecution is going to use this document for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, just a moment, why does the Prosecutor request that we do not discuss it in front of the witnesses when his witnesses were there, he said why should the witnesses go out? That was the Prosecution's position when their witnesses came here to testify. It is all in the record, and now he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. changes that the situation be reversed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you first, sir, it may be, Your Honour, in some of these background personal issues I suppose unfortunately we will have to be -- well maybe these aren't identifying, I will try because I don't think anyone could hold a number of these positions. I'll try without being in private session. Sir, in listening to your testimony I just want to talk a little bit about your military background and positions because some of that was not clear to me. You said that you first joined the HV, that is the Croatian Army, as a student volunteer in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And at that period of time, how long did you remain in the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Until April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as of the time you left the Croatian Army, sir, what rank or position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At the time, I did not hold a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you joined the Croatian Army, as you've described, was that your first involvement in a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. Before that, I served in the regular army for 14 months, in the former state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you obtain any certain -- any particular rank during that period of service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say -- I mean it may not be the exact terminology used by the Croatian Army but what many people would consider your rank do you remember that during that entire time was perhaps a foot soldier or private?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. I was a foot soldier. I had some duties in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you ever attend a military academy in the course of your military career?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. I apologise. After the war, I was at the Croatian military school and I was at the war school of the Croatian Army school, and I was at the command school of the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And those were all after the conflict primarily with the Muslims in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you went to return to Siroki Brijeg and became involved in a unit there, did you continue to hold any rank or membership or position in the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. I did not have a rank, nor -- when I arrived in Siroki Brijeg, I had duty as an instructor of training, of drills.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then sometime after leaving the HVO, did you become a member of the Croatian Army, the HV, again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: During the operations to liberate the Northwestern Bosnia, that was in 1995, after the Tudjman-Izetbegovic agreement signed in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. My only question is: So was it in 1995 that you joined again the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: After all the wars that took place in the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I wanted to resolve my status in the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was the highest rank, sir, that you ever obtained in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: The last rank in the HVO was general --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move to a private session? These things are -- can identify this witness and can I ask my learned friend to make sure not to repeat something like that? Because there are no hundreds of generals in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you request, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my only question about this document, and again, please don't mention your name or any other specifics about the document other than the things that I'll be careful to ask you about, but at some point were you granted disability benefits based on your military service? That's just simply if you can assist us, please, just yes or no. Sir, in terms of the content of the document I'm only going to ask you one question on the second English page or for that matter it may be simply easier for everyone's attention to the next page, third page in the English version, just simply a list of essentially information 1 through 9, if you could find the page, sir, the last page, of the Croatian language version that has a number of items 1 through 9, and I just simply ask you to confirm that is it correct, sir, and Mr. President, I don't think this information is sufficient to identify a specific person, if counsel or the Court disagrees I'm sure they will guide me -- is it correct, sir, that as a member of the Convicts Battalion, you were wounded on the 19th of January, 1993, in Gornji Vakuf? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: At the time, I was not a member of the Convicts Battalion. I was a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. As a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG, were you wounded in Gornji Vakuf on the 19th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I was slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as a member of either the Convicts Battalion or the Baja Kraljevic ATG, were you also wounded in Doljani on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. I was not wounded on the 16th of April. Again, I assert that I was a member of the Baja Kraljevic unit. I was hit by a bullet in the Motorola that I was carrying, on the belt, and it scratched me. It tore off the antenna, and this did not prevent me from continuing fighting in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask it, I don't want to quarrel with you as much as possible about these things, is it correct that you were struck, you or something on your body was struck by a bullet on the 16th of April, 1993, in the vicinity of Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. That was south from Doljani towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, then, that as a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG were you then again wounded or injured to some -- to any degree on the 20th of June, 1993, in a place called Boksevica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. In the Baja Kraljevic unit, I was wounded on Boksevica on the 20 April -- no, 20 June, 1993. And Mr. Mandic and I were wounded at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, you were granted a -- as a result of this -- as indicated in this document, at least, you were granted a 40 per cent permanent disability. Now, sir, you're not -- some of the qualifications you've made in the last few minutes, you're not indicating in any way, are you, that there was anything false about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: These injuries were slight injuries, and it is correct that I was wounded on Boksevica, and in the Matkovic sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The extent and nature of your injuries as you've told us about this morning which I appreciate, was that -- would those commonly be characterised then under the HVO benefits system as resulting in a 40 per cent permanent disability?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I never took this disability, although during that stage, when all those who had been wounded were being registered and -- I wanted this to be recorded for the posterity that during the fight for the Croatian people, I was at the disposal, and that I had gone through certain stages and that I did experience -- I did experience the feeling of being hit by a bullet in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I have the usher's assistance, please, and if I may suggest, perhaps with the usher's assistance to keep the papers straight, if the binder could be shown to the witness so we could move rather quickly through about five or six exhibits, if that's possible? The next exhibit I specifically want to direct his attention to, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. witness's attention to is P173.3. The numbers are on the English version, the way we prepare exhibits for the Prosecution in trial is to put the numbers on the English page, not the B/C/S page. There should be a number in the upper right corner P173.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, before I ask you any other document -- excuse me, questions about this exhibit, did you ever know a man in the Baja Kraljevic unit called Goran Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Goran Pavlovic I know. I can't remember whether he was in the Convicts Battalion, but in any case, he is a guy who was wounded in October, 1992, south of Mostar somewhere around Vrada -- I think the name of the place is Vranjevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to refer to the item because the page numbers in the English and Croatian versions may be different. On the list, if you can please finds item number 87? Is that your name on this list, indicating the rank? It's not on the ELMO. I'm not going to ask to you state your name, please, but is that you on the list indicated as captain? Number 87. Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. This is my name, but what is this form? What time does it -- what date is it all?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you direct your attention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes, I see, 15 September, 1992. I could not have the rank of a captain at the time, because at that time, there were no ranks in the HVO units. There were some markings of the duty, of certain commanders, of brigades, or battalions, or companies, but the first ranks were conferred upon individuals, I believe in early 1994, so that this here is not true. This rank of captain or any other rank indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, I understand you disagree with that, sir, but let me direct your attention please now next to item 77, Goran Pavlovic, and if you will just -- taking the document at face value, sir, just taking what is stated on the document at face value, can you assist the Chamber in any information you can provide as to why the rank for Mr. Pavlovic was, apparently the original rank suggested was marked out, above it appears to be the abbreviation for Colonel, Pukov, and then to the right of that is written the name, the rank for major, and the words "Tuta's personal request." Can you shed any light as to why Mr. Naletilic wanted this man to be given this particular rank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Well, since Goran Pavlovic was a member, and I believe one of those lads that belonged to the old team, he possibly spoke with Mr. Naletilic, probably to -- if at that time he had already been wounded and I said that he had been wounded, so perhaps he asked somehow to have his status resolved but I repeat, as for the ranks at that time, there were no ranks at that time. You can go to Narodni Novine in that period and you will never see a decision on the ranks, on the granting of ranks at the time, so I do not agree with this promotion to colonel or major and I do not know what it said underneath this, this which has been crossed out, and as for this request of the gentleman, if that is -- if of all these men who are listed here, here, the signature, or if it is, if Mr. Naletilic did write that, then it could be the good intention, perhaps, at Mr. Pavlovic's request. I don't know if my answer satisfies you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are going to have to move on. I would have to just put it to you, sir, so the record is clear, that it's the Prosecution case that there are a number of documents from this time which in fact indicate ranks but I understand your position. Can I ask you, please, to look at P564.2? Very quickly, sir, if you can assist, I simply want you to confirm, are you the second person listed on that list, and is that accurate information as of the date of this document, 12 August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I don't know to -- how accurate is this information, if it is dated August, 1993, and if as a signatory, we have commander Viktor Markotic, "Civi," so I do not think this information is accurate and I do not know what is this report meant for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, is it correct that as of the 12th of August, 1993, you were a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG and in fact, you were someone who came from the Siroki Brijeg municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is true, I was born in Siroki Brijeg, and I still live there, and the unit, Baja Kraljevic, was not in the staff of the Siroki Brijeg municipality and what it says here, those who belong to Siroki Brijeg municipality, and therefore do not need to have been sent mobilisation papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention to Exhibit P934? And sir, this states that it is a list of the dead and wounded during the execution of past operations and the ranks of the Convicts Battalion and the Baja Kraljevic ATG, and then there is a list of some 53 names. Are you number 22 on this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber, please, within this particular document, why are the Convicts Battalion and the Baja Kraljevic ATG intermixed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I don't know when this document was created because there is no date here, no number, no class, no signature. Men -- I know men in this list. Marko Lovric, I know when he was killed, Franjo Pastelek was in ATG Baja Kraljevic and he was killed in November, 1992. Danko Radman, Stanislav Kraljevic, I mean I know those men. And I do not know who wrote this and who was this list sent to, and why were these put together. But I do know, and I put it to you, that Baja Kraljevic, that unit, looked after its dead and its killed, and that the Convicts Battalion unit did the same. I don't know if this can be of any help to you. The military code of the Convicts Battalion was 1717. And the military code of the Baja Kraljevic was 1724. And here in the heading, I do not see it say anywhere that particular fact. I don't see it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I've given you the document I have. I understand the concerns you've expressed I cannot give you something I do not have. But isn't it true, sir that the Convicts Battalion and the Baja Kraljevic were so closely identified one with the other that it was common for them to be listed together or for the member of the Convicts Battalion to be commonly referred to as a member of the Baja Kraljevic unit and vice versa, a member of the Baja Kraljevic unit to be identified as someone with the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I have already said that they are two different units with their different military codes, different markings, and surely, men who were in those units could not identify themselves with some other unit. Members of Baja Kraljevic were its members, and they said so proudly. But there were members in Baja Kraljevic who in the early stages were with the Convicts Battalion. So that possibly there could have been some men who said, yes, I'm a member of the Convicts Battalion, and so on. But it was a very clear in those units themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to please look at P738?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, this will be the last document we are using before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very good, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can just confirm for me, this is another states that it is another listing of persons of the Baja Kraljevic ATG dated the 4th of January, 1994, and are you the person listed in item number 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if such confirmation is sought, then the witness should be allowed to read and check every name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think so. I think the witness is provided with that document already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer would be that Mr. Predrag Mandic, the first one on the list, was at that time appointed commander of the 1st Battalion of the 2nd Guards Brigade set up in November -- in December, 1992, and Josip, I'm here, Josip is it with that brigade, Slaven Lasic is with the new brigade, and of -- and a large number of men from this list are members of that brigade so that this document, I cannot consider it an authentic document because most of the members were members of the 2nd Guards Brigade of the Mostar HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: To finish up, I know we are at the break time but, sir, for the purposes of a document like this would you not agree that this indicates, for instance, the members of these particular individuals in their prior unit up to the time in early 1994 that it became part of the 2nd Guards Brigade? Isn't that what this document indicates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I do not know. If I said that the 2nd Guards Brigade was established and if in its development and the establishment and order on its foundation said, and that the selection of men in the command of that brigade had already been carried out, Mr. Mandic has just after January at the time when he was the commander of the indicated unit, Baja Kraljevic, he was wounded after that, he was severely wounded in the end of that month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's beyond the scope of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President we can stop there for the break, if it suits the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can ask you to look next at Exhibit 812. Sir, this document is titled, "list of members of the Convicts Battalion registered in the Siroki Brijeg Defence office." It appears to be dated the 24th of July, 1996. I want to start please I want to directs your attention because you've mentioned this several times up in the upper left part of the first page it says, "Military post 1717." Just to confirm again you've said this morning that 1717 was the military code for the Convicts Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is correct that the military post code of the Convicts Battalion was 1717.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that you were listed in this list as -- at item 30, 30?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: That is my name but I do not know what would I be doing in this list, if this document is of 1996, as you said, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, in the Croatian language original will you please look at your name, item 30? Is that not your signature in the far right column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And is this document not prepared over the name, I'm not suggesting anything about the handwriting at the moment, but over the name Mladen Naletilic, Tuta? Is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. On this form, there is the name, yes, it is written here, Mladen Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Under the title on the form of commander, authorised person, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is not correct that at that time, Mr. Naletilic was the commander, authorised person. It is possible, if the Defence office was comparing some documentation perhaps it relates to 1992, if they were trying to update some documentation for the Siroki Brijeg archives. In that case, it is -- then it would be correct if it refers to 1992. But since this is the 24th of July, 1996, at that time Mr. Naletilic had -- held no command office. And it is also possible that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm sorry I do not want to interrupt you but I'm trying to move us along but please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: It is possible, I remember that Mr. Naletilic, at some point in time, was in the Siroki Brijeg municipality. That is in the municipal hall of Siroki Brijeg, whether he was deputy mayor or something. So perhaps that motivated him to put down certain things which date to 1992. That would be my comment with regard to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not with regard to that document but just generally in terms of your examination, you said, you were quite categorical in saying you had never heard anyone use the terminology, Tuta's ATG or Tuta's men, that sort of thing, but sir, isn't it quite common, wouldn't it be quite normal when people in referring to a particular unit might refer to it buy the commander's name such as for example someone in this courtroom might describe this court as Judge Lieu's courtroom. It may be Trial Chamber I but isn't it correct that people would commonly refer to a unit by the commander's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Possibly. It is possible that at that time, somebody addressed somebody or referred to somebody, perhaps within that context, meaning all of us who were at that time together with Mr. Naletilic in the Convicts Battalion. Perhaps somebody from that time, and within the context of that time, but I do not remember that anyone ever addressed me or called me Tuta's man or Tuta's boy or Tutici and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of your comments about Mr. Naletilic being for unity of Muslims or Bosniaks and Croats, you don't mean that in the way that they were equal, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I know that in 1992, Mr. Naletilic, if I may put it that way, socialised and was welcome amongst the Muslim population in Herzegovina, or more specifically in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when you say unity, isn't it fair to say that people like Mr. Naletilic and other members of the senior Bosnian Croat leadership, they meant unity was fine as long as it was under HVO control, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer you in that way. That is to just say whether this is correct. I think it is rather the other way around. In the struggle against the common enemy, common aggressor, I think the Croats and Muslims cooperated very well because a large number of the population chased away from other parts of Bosnia, from Eastern Bosnia, were very well received in Herzegovina, and there were no particular problems there. Now, there could be some later things behind which was some other motive but I can also give you my view on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, unfortunately again we are pressed for time, sir. You said that you arrived in Doljani during the time of the Sovici-Doljani action, that you arrived in Doljani and Mr. Naletilic was already there. Can you clarify, please, what day or date -- I guess not day in the week but what date was it when you arrived in Doljani and Mr. Naletilic was already there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: We found Mr. Naletilic there on the 19th, in the afternoon, in the village of Doljani but we as the unit arrived there on the 17th of April, in the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. That answers my question, sir, forgive me but again I just wanted to know what date that was and I appreciate you're indicating the 19th of April. Then when you say that the Baja Kraljevic unit withdrew to Siroki Brijeg, can you again -- and you said Mr. Naletilic was in the car in front of you, and again my only question is, can you clarify -- identify that date? What date was it that you with drew to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I think it was the 19th of April, the 19th of April, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it accurate to say, sir, that you, you personally, did not go back to the Doljani-Sovici area after that, at least not in April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: To the area of Sovici and Doljani, we as the unit intervened there in July, 1993. When the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in the interests of time I'm trying to give you very direct questions, please. After the 19th of April, when you said you withdrew to Siroki Brijeg, did you go back to the Doljani-Sovici area during the month of April, not July, during the month of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. We did not return to the area of Sovici and Doljani in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, is it correct that around the early October, around early October, 1993, you were given command of the 3rd HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness please be shown Exhibit 621? Can you confirm, sir, that this is a record, an HVO record, indicating your promotion or naming to that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
