utterances.text: I never saw this document before, because this is a proposal by the Main Staff of the HVO to the Defence Minister, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it also indicates?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Scott, can we please redact this and make sure that the witness is not identified? Can we redact his position, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's a fair request, Your Honour. Perhaps we should go to private session just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, sir, and you may have touched on this in your direct examination, but I'd like to confirm, that unit was based largely on or built from, if you will, the Convicts Battalion? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Not only of the members of the Convicts Battalion. During this reorganisation, four guards brigades were formed and 2nd Guards Brigade consisted of all the units in -- from zone of responsibility of Mostar. So they became professional. So the military police, the Convicts Battalion, the Baja Kraljevic, effectively all the smaller-sized units which belonged to their respective municipalities, they from then on became integral parts of that guard unit -- guard brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did that include, sir, the Vinko Martinovic's unit known as ATG Vinko Skrobo? Excuse me, my apology.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. His unit also became incorporated in the 2nd Guards Brigade, that is Mr. Martinovic's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And sir, isn't it correct to say that Vinko Skrobo unit was incorporated into the 2nd Guards Brigade because it was part of the Convicts Battalion? That was incorporated into the 2nd Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. The Vinko Skrobo unit had its zone of responsibility, its commander, and it was not a part of the Convicts unit and it did not -- it was not incorporated into the brigade as such. As soon as the 2nd Brigade was formed, all the smaller units were dismantled and from then on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter missed a large part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, one large part, sentence, did not -- did not get translated because the witness was too fast. So can -- when he was explaining about the smaller units incorporated and that they ranked from -- squads, platoons, and other smaller units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you may reanswer that question. I'm afraid that the interpreter might have lost something in your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the 2nd Guards Brigade incorporated the units from the area of responsibility of the Mostar territory, those units which were active in either professional or semi-professional capacity were incorporated into the guard brigade. And obviously, all of them were first dismantled, they did not remain as they were previously, they were transformed, and adapted to the new establishment, and that is from squad, infantry squad, infantry platoon, all the other elements that guards brigade have, the artillery, anti-artillery, and all the other services accompanying such a professional unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have to end it there. Based on what you told us about your military career I think it's fair to say that many by some measures would consider it quite successful, which causes me to ask you do you consider yourself or that you were a good officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it is not for me to say that. It is for others to say. But people with whom I worked and my superiors probably made a selection based on my abilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's fair to say, you were promoted up through the ranks to increasingly senior positions. You were, if we had time, you received numerous awards or commendations from the Republic of Croatia, I think at least five or six, so many people considered you a good officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in your role as an experienced and apparently much promoted officer, did you consider that you took all steps to exercise command and control over the units and soldiers under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, when we are talking about different times and different circumstances that I personally found myself in, obviously that all the knowledge that I had acquired in the universities and the abilities I tried to implement to incorporate in the media in the environment that was called the army or the army potential, and I also to a large extent, I believe, that I succeeded in my intentions, but obviously, there were, in such a mobilised situation, when -- if we look at the years 1992 and 1993, it is possible that there were some deviations by individuals who could not have been selected for their characteristics, for their psychological traumas for their previous war experiences, did they lose somebody to the war, did somebody, a member of mayor family got killed? And only in 1994, I believe that the military vertical and horizontal chain of commands became established in the proper sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, because of the time I'm going to be quite selective in the documents that I can direct you to so I'll only pick one of this particular group. If you could please look at P703.4? [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I'm not sure that at the time I had tools available to me. It was improvisation on my part as the commander. I improvised some things in order to impose some disciplinary measures. One of them was a pay cut. In order to draw the attention of other members of this unit to the fact that I can take disciplinary measure if some deviations were found in the communication within the units but in this particular case, I would like to say that this is a reserve brigade, which was based effectively on mobilisation. Its units were mobilised so there was no selection of people. People could not be segregated based on their character traits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I need to go forward. My only other question to you about this document, is you indicate in your order, you characterised whatever the underlying conduct was as involving a serious violation, I think in one or two instances a place a term you use. I know this is sometime ago but I just wonder if you can assist the Chamber if you recall what conduct of these two men was being punished at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I can't remember what disciplinary measure and based on what I imposed by this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's understandable, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I don't want to say something that does not reflect the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it a fact that during 1993, in the conflict between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosniaks or the Muslims, and that Muslim prisoners were widely used in forced labour by the HVO? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Yes. There were instances of units using those prisoners who were conscripts, but I think it was in their areas of responsibility for some works. I don't know what exactly they did but I did hear that there were such instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, sir, units under your immediate command made widespread use of Muslim prisoners in forced labour, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Which units are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, for instance, the 3rd Brigade that you were commanding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Which unit of the 3rd brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, again, sir, unfortunately because of the statement constraints if I can ask you to look at Exhibit P935, I believe -- it's a very, very thick exhibit, Mr. President, and I don't know if it was put in all the binders or because of the volume it may have not but do you have it, Mr. Usher, do you in your -- it appears that you do. I can see it from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you'll please look at Exhibit P935. It's a very voluminous collection of a form, what appears to be a standard form. I can't pretend that I've looked through each one of these but the vast majority of the pages seem to bear your signature as the approving officer. Isn't that true? And as I leaf, just so the record is clear and I'm not accused of misleading anyone, as I leaf through here again now admitted there are, there are other signatures besides yours but I think it's fair to say a very, very substantial number percentage of this bundle bears your signature, doesn't it? While you're considering that, sir, if you want to look, I understand you may want to look at the documents, let me assist the Chamber and counsel, Mr. President, there is one translation of the form on the top page and we think the form itself is always -- wealth substantially the same, which seems to say this: Order for requisitioning prisoners, name of unit, work location, number of prisoners, the date, the first and last name, person in charge, ID number, taken over by, and then to the right of that, approved by. Sir, isn't it true that your signature is on a substantial number of these forms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I don't know that I have signed such orders but this could be my signature. I was not the person in charge of the military prison and I could not issue approvals, I could issue requests, but approvals for the requisition of these prisoners, I did not have such authority but if you will allow me, Your Honours, I would like to mention that I joined the 3rd brigade at the beginning of the month and that I had a takeover or the handover of the brigade between the 4th and the 20th of October, and that at that time, that brigade had its communication, its life, and within that one month or two months that I had spent in the brigade, I acted very little. I may have overlooked some things, and I will allow that that may have happened, and I would like to mention that the -- one of the units of the 3rd Brigade was in the sector of the defence of the town. That was the 4th Battalion which was under the command of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm trying very hard to finish this cross-examination. If we can just look at one example, the very first one, which -- if you want to look -- confirming the last four digits in the number that's marked on the top right corner of the page, 7946, that's your signature, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: This could be my signature but there is no date on this -- whatever it is, the order, there is no date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. Isn't it true that you knew that not only were prisoners being used but many of them were being taken out of the most hostile conditions and many of them were being wounded and killed or otherwise abused? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I don't believe this to be true, for the following reason. The 3rd Brigade was of a mixed composition up to the month of May or June of that same year, while its commander was Ivan Primorac. The battalions in this brigade, the 8th Battalion, the 9th Battalion, all of them were made up of Muslims and Croats in the ratio of 40 to 60 maybe, and they acted jointly against the common enemy, and then this early stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry, I wasn't asking about the composition of the units. Let me direct your attention, please, to an exhibit which is marked as P657.1, and sir, I'll have to tell you that the cover, the table or summary that's been prepared in the top is not yet been translated, but attached -- attached to it or the Croatian language documents, the ten documents that correspond, the entries, so if you want to confirm presumably you will, what the table is based upon, you can look at the attached B/C/S document, sir. And I'm going to suggest to you, in the interests of time, that all of these indicate that these soldiers were taken out on your request or under your approval if you look at the Croatian language documents, I believe you will see in all instances in the first or second line, your name. Is that correct? Sir, I'm going to tell you again so that we can move forward in these reports there are many indications of detainees being wounded, some allegedly escaped, in one instance it indicates that a group of detainees, item 6, came back from labour having been badly beaten. This was a widely known practice, wasn't it, sir,? And you knew this was going on, you knew prisoners were being taken out exposed to the most dangerous conditions and many soldiers -- many of them, none of these indicated as being killed but in fact many were being wounded and killed, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: As far as this document goes, which indicates that I was the person in charge, and that the prison warden says that it is on my request, I don't see any such request here. But I will comment upon the military prisoners, prisoners of war. I can tell you that the other side, the Muslim side, wanted to draw to the military prisoners to the -- front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but we have a few minutes left and my question was not what happened often the Muslim side but what happened to these particular prisoners and to Muslim prisoners in general. Sir, would you please look at Exhibit P644? You're familiarising yourself with that, sir, isn't it true that on the 14th of October, 1993, General Milivoj Petkovic, the deputy commander of the HVO Main Staff by that date ordered item 1, "I hereby prohibit the use of prisoners to carry out any type of work in the brigade zones of responsibility." I assume this order found its way to you, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: Possibly, possibly, it could all be accurate, but I'd like to comment on this order. I repeat that at that time it was the time of the handover of duty between the former commander, between the future commander and my takeover, and this whole procedure lasted about 15 or 20 days, and it was at that time that this order arrived. So I cannot say that at that time, I mean I joined the unit with war experience. We had no contact with any prisoners or any captured persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I understand your answer and I think it's clear, I think you've given it I'm not trying to be unfair to you. This was a changeover period at least at the beginning of the taking command of the brigade. I understand that, my question to you is this: Are you telling this Chamber that you were unaware of General Petkovic's order not to use prisoners in forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No. That is not what I wanted to say. Here under item 2 it says if however this sort of activities is allowed the permit shall be issued by the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you telling this Chamber, then, sir, that in all the instances in this thick bundle of documents, which covers approximately a month or two, that all those were approved by the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: No, no. That is not what I want to say at all. But there was the military prison, there were those investigative authorities, and clearly, any deviation of the order that had been issued would have been sanctioned at the relevant level of authority if it had to deal with the breaches of discipline or non-compliance with orders, whatever happened in those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you usher please assist in providing the witness or directing him to P686.1? Yes, there should be a Croatian language version there, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, again our time is limited. There appears to be a report issued by Josip Praljak, the deputy warden of the central military prison, often referred to as the Heliodrom. On the 24th of November, 1993. I want to direct your attention to -- try to assist you as much as I can in terms of the Croatian version -- I think on the Croatian version, sir, if you will look down to about the fourth paragraph on that document and in the English version, Mr. President, approximately the third paragraph on the second page, starting with the words, "With the approval of." Again I'm not going to use the witness's name and, witness, I'll caution you not to use your own name in the document -- in reference to this document which of course will have to be puts under seal. Does the document, does Mr. Praljak's report not indicate that with your approval, the 3rd Brigade commander, the warden made an exception for that particular brigade as regards the release of prisoners for labour, it being clear that the detainees were to work with in the barracks compound at the following task: Skipping down, "however, derelictions occurred as follows." The request says, 'the barracks compound' but they take detainees outside the compound where escapes by detainees, deaths and woundings have occurred. Reports on all of this have been submitted to our superiors." So isn't it further true, sir, that very deliberately, it was being indicated these prisoners were only taken out to work around the barracks but in fact they were being taken out for forced labour at other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I think that this has to do, as it says here, if this document is authentic, and for me this is the first time to see it, to see this document, and this report, because I did not get this report from the prison warden. If there was -- if I, as the commander of that brigade, have committed some error then I should have received this report. At that time, on the other hand, no other suggestive document which would have drawn my attention, that I erred in the performance of my command duties, I received nothing else. If this had to do with sending prisoners to work, within the barracks compound, and then be engaged in logistics, kitchen workshop, cleaning the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I think the Chamber has your answer. I must move on. Did you ever issue orders, sir, for Muslim property and houses to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honour, I merely wanted to ask, I do not know, we have only ten minutes to go. There may be redirect. You may also have questions. We are not in session tomorrow. I do not know. It will be up to you. Shall we have to keep this witness until Monday? I'd really like to finish him today, because the Prosecutor, you see, I never objected to the time of the cross-examination, I never objected to the duration of the cross-examination but that time is long overdue for the end of it. I don't know. Can we stay a little bit longer perhaps today? Because I'm sure that you will have some questions too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I don't think could finish this witness today. Since we just have a few minutes left, which is five or seven minutes left. So this witness has to stay here over the weekend. Mr. Scott, could I ask you to ask one more question? Then we'll stop. We have to stop a little bit earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think the Chamber will have been able to observe this morning, I hope that I've really tried to go as quickly as possible. And not be discourteous to the witness. And if I have, if he believes I have been discourteous to him then I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention to one last document for the day, sir, excuse me, my apology before Mr. Krsnik expressed his concern, my question to you was this: Did you ever authorise or order the confiscation of Muslim property? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: I do not remember ever ordering or commanding the confiscation of any property.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the last document I'd like you to look at very briefly so we can meet the President's schedule is Exhibit 708.2. Now, sir, before anyone else says so, I'm going to say right off that that signature does not look like other signatures that seem to be yours, so I'm not suggesting, I don't want to be understood as suggesting that that's necessarily your signature but this is an order issued over your name and over your position, is it not, to -- on the 4th of December, 1993, to seize various items from Muslim houses in the locality of Buna for the needs of the 3rd Battalion, 1st Company? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: This document is not accurate because I did not sign it and this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you assist us, please, is that the name or the signature of a person, a deputy or a person that you can assist the Chamber with? I certainly don't know the signature but can you assist us, sir? Do you recognise that name as being one of your deputies or someone that you worked with at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: This is the 3rd Battalion, 1st Company of the 3rd Brigade which was in the area of responsibility Buna Ortijes. And well, now, this document, who could have signed it, I can say and I say it under full responsibility before this Honourable Court that this is not my signature and that I cannot remember really because I was the commander of that brigade for a very short time and I cannot really remember who signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, my last question, Mr. President, is, and again I'm not going to argue with you about the signature but isn't it true, sir, this was done based on your authority? If you didn't sign it, you knew this was being done, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM
utterances.text: How could I know that this was being done? At that time, that is December, 1993, I was engaged intensively in the implementation of the task that I was given, and that was the reorganisation of units into guards brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm sorry to say that we did not finish your testimony today, that you have to stay in The Hague until next Monday. As I did with other witnesses, I have to remind you that during your stay in The Hague, you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anyone about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the end of the sentence, we are sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The usher will show you out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We might have some scheduling problems for the next few weeks sitting time. This Trial Chamber will get in touch with the Registrar to sort out all the problems. As I promised to Mr. Meek that we will render our decision concerning the recess, we will try our best to hand it down tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, I only do this because you need to leave the bench, but I do believe I have an obligation to counsel and I want to be fair about this. Mr. Meek asked me today again about your position so I want to be clear about this. I think it is clear but let me be absolutely clear. In concept, if all of the things being equal we would not object to the breaks. I think we've tried to make that clear if it assists counsel in some ways and we have been going at a rather full pace in many respects but the Prosecution's concern was that there would not be some shortening of the schedule in such a way that it would come back and affect the manner of examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have received your written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In any event, I had told Mr. Meek that I would make that point made and I wanted to be -- keep my word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
